column2: Mr. Kobayashi was there.
He sat on the floor with his back against the wall and his legs stretched out.
A kitchen knife was plunged into Mr. Kobayashi's belly, and the floor where he sat had become a sea of blood.
He must have tried to pull it out himself; both hands gripped the knife as if he'd committed seppuku.
Stomach acid rose and I covered my mouth with my hand.
I was about to be sick, so I rushed for the bathroom.
The moment I opened the bathroom door, something fell toward me.
A bloodstained hand.
I nearly let out a pathetic squeal.
Bright red blood was spattered across the bathroom walls and sink.
Kyoko, naked, lay dead in the doorway with her head resting on the edge of the bathtub.
And her vacant eyes, like glass beads, stared fixedly at me.
This was what had made {n2} scream, unable to bear it.
And to {n2}, they were her blood relatives, her uncle and aunt.
How great a shock she must have suffered.
Thinking of it, the fact that {n2} had kept her sanity might mean a strong will at work, one that didn't show in her looks.
I wanted to get back to {n2} as fast as possible.
I backed away two or three steps, and when the two bodies were out of sight, I ran headlong.
I could no longer walk slowly and cautiously.
I just wanted to get away from there, even a moment sooner.
As I passed the back door, I noticed something like blood on the doorknob.
Why in a place like this...?{r}{P}
It bothered me, and I stopped.
Looking closely, there wasn't just the knob; there were dark, blood-like marks near the floor too.
judged that in the present situation it was a trivial matter and decided to ignore it.
Ordinarily I'd have had to find out where Toshio had gone.
But right now, it no longer mattered.
I raced through the lounge and flew up the stairs.
It surely took less than ten seconds to reach the office girls' room.
Open up!{r}{P}”
I shouted as I knocked.
I heard a bit of arguing inside, but the door opened right away.
“Thank goodness...
you're safe.”
{n2} flew out and threw her arms around my neck.
{n2} had been that worried about me...
That made me happy, and my fear eased a little.
“Did Mrs. Kayama
come here?{r}{P}”
“No.
She hasn't...”
“I see...
Then maybe she went back to her own room.”
I hoped no one had attacked her on the way back...
A nasty thought crossed my mind.
“You didn't hear any strange noises or voices,
did you?{r}{P}”
{n2} silently shook her head.
Then she was probably fine.
I counted the people still alive.
The three girls,
me,
and Haruko...
That was all.
Only six, and everyone except me was a woman.
To prevent any more victims, we really had to all stay together.
I approached Mr. Kayama's room door.
“Mrs. Kayama!{r}{P}
Mrs. Kayama, are you there?{r}{P}{p}Please come out!{r}{P}{p}It's safer to be together!{r}{P}”
While I waited, fidgeting, the door slowly opened.
Haruko stood there with a face like a ghost.
“Come over here, please.”
I took her arm and half-dragged her to the room where everyone was.
Then I shut the door and locked it.
The three girls huddled in the corner of the room as if protecting themselves from us.
But they didn't seem to want to throw us out.
Maybe {n2} had convinced them that the killer was Toshio.
“We're the only ones still alive.{r}{p}Except for Toshio.”
Saying it aloud made it ring strangely hollow.
Were they really all dead?{r}{P}
Might I have mistaken what I saw?{r}{P}
I felt as if I'd wandered not into reality but into a movie or TV drama.
“...Toshio killed my husband?”
Haruko murmured without emotion, standing stock-still.
“I can't think of anything else.{r}{p}...There's no one left who could have, and Toshio was ready to kill Mr. Kayama, wasn't he?{r}{P}”
Even as I said it, I realized something was off.
“...Maybe Toshio
thought he was avenging her!{r}{P}”
{n2} looked up as if struck.
“Avenging?{r}{P}
Midori?{r}{P}{p}...Then who did those awful things to the Kobayashis?{r}{P}”
“...Toshio,
wouldn't you say?”
“Why would he have to do something so awful?!{r}{P}”
“But...
we gave the cellar key to Uncle.”
...The key!{r}{P}
That was right.
Without the key, that door couldn't be opened.
...So he killed even the two Kobayashis just to kill Mr. Kayama?{r}{P}
“That's insane...
that's insane!{r}{P}”
But thinking it through, it all fit.
Mr. Kayama had killed Mr. Tanaka and Midori.
And Toshio killed the Kobayashis, took the key, opened the cellar door, and killed Mr. Kayama...
If that was right, wasn't there no danger to us anymore?{r}{P}
Unless Toshio had completely lost his mind and meant to kill at random, he had no reason to kill me, {n2} or the girls.
But since he'd killed even the blameless Kobayashis, shouldn't we judge that he was already out of his mind?{r}{P}
Remembering that gruesome scene, I felt nausea rise again.
“...What do we do
...from here...?{r}{P}”
{n2} asked in a voice barely audible.
“...We hold out here until morning.”
“And when morning comes, then what?{r}{P}”
“...The weather will probably improve a bit, and maybe the phone will work.{r}{p}Someone...
someone might come.”
Maybe, maybe...
Even as I said it, I knew it was all wishful thinking.
“...What if
...what if the weather and the phone haven't changed at all...?{r}{P}”
“...The weather will clear up eventually.{r}{p}Then we can go down the mountain.”
I knew it wasn't that simple.
Even if the blizzard stopped, the road wouldn't be passable without snow removal.
And we couldn't get the car out of the parking lot on our own.
No, the car had probably been buried in snow long ago, maybe impossible even to find.
Everyone seemed to be thinking the same thing; the oppressive mood only deepened.
The shock and terror we'd suffered came from seeing violent death, something we never encounter in real life.
There was nowhere left to run...
Shut in a small room, listening to the wind howl, I felt crushed by that thought.
I might be killed senselessly, just like the others...
That fear nearly suffocated me.
Yes, like Mr. Kayama...!{r}{P}
Like Mr. Kobayashi...!{r}{P}
And perhaps like Mr. Tanaka...!{r}{P}
Staying shut in the room was surely the safest thing.
But Toshio was free to walk around outside...{p}watching us from out there, and the moment he saw an opening, he might attack...?{r}{P}!{r}{P}
The thought made me frantic.
I began to feel it might be safer to run somewhere.
How long had we spent in that silence?
It felt like hours had passed, so I looked at my watch...{p}but it wasn't even five yet.
Haruko went to the window, wiped the glass with her hand and peered out.
“...It's too dark to tell, but it seems the same as ever...”
The three girls, dark circles under their eyes and faces haggard, huddled shoulder to shoulder with their eyes closed.
They might have been half asleep.
{n2}'s face was in terrible shape too.
Eyelids swollen from crying,
bloodshot eyes, deep dark circles, disheveled hair...
My face was probably much the same.
Haruko, who had lost her husband, looked the most normal of all.
They say when you're truly sad the tears won't come, but she seemed not even to have decided yet whether she was sad.
...Wait.
Suddenly a suspicion arose.
I had reasoned that Mr. Kayama had killed Mr. Tanaka and Midori.
But if Mr. Kayama could do it, so could Haruko, who'd claimed to be in the room with him.
Couldn't they have been accomplices?
If so, Haruko could muddy everything by making it look like Toshio killed Mr. Kayama.
It could look like Toshio was the killer of everyone, or like he had taken revenge on Mr. Kayama, the killer.
...Yes,
just as I had thought.
I desperately suppressed the fear that suddenly surged.
It's all right.
It's all right.
There was nothing to worry about.
Even if that were so, as long as I didn't let my guard down, there was no way a woman like that could kill me.
Besides, if that reasoning was right, she had no need to commit any more crimes.
Killing anyone further would waste the effort of pinning it on Mr. Kayama or Toshio.
...Ah, I couldn't make sense of anything anymore.
What on earth had happened?
Who was the killer?
Was the danger really over?
What should we do now?
The nightmarish sights, one after another, had left me unable to tell what was fact and what was imagination.
Then a strange sound came from somewhere.
An electronic chime, “ding-dong.”
“...What was
that?{r}{P}”
{n2} asked, her unease plain, but of course I had no idea.
“It sounded...
like the door chime, but...”
Of course that couldn't be.
In this blizzard, before dawn, no one would come to an inn in the mountains like this, or could.
But the chime-like sound rang out again.
Once more.
And once more.
We looked at each other.
“Noooo!{r}{P}”
Keiko screamed and threw herself face down on the bed.
“Y-y-your lost lambs...{g}
save, save us...”
Trembling, she kept repeating her prayer.
The chime sounded again.
Kanako stood up abruptly.
“Someone...
someone has come to help us!{r}{P}”
She rushed to the door and tried to open it.
I thought,
No help could possibly come; this was a trap.
“Wait!{r}{P}
No one could possibly be coming!{r}{P}”
I hurriedly grabbed her arm.
“...But
...it's ringing!{r}{P}
Listen!{r}{P}”
Indeed, the chime kept ringing.
“...Our Father in heaven...”
Keiko, perhaps thinking a ghost was ringing it, raised her prayer louder.
Her figure praying with her hair in disarray, and her voice, made the eerie scene all the more unsettling.
Irritated, I said to Kanako.
“Maybe Toshio is ringing it!{r}{P}”
“Why would he do that?!{r}{P}”
“I don't know!{r}{p}How should I know!{r}{P}”
I was confused myself and didn't know what I was saying.
“Right, maybe it's to lure us out.{r}{p}No!{r}{P}
Maybe something blown by the wind is hitting the intercom.”
Whether such a thing could really happen
I merely blurted out whatever came to mind.
“I can't believe that!{r}{P}{p}What if we all keep quiet and the person who came to help leaves?!{r}{P}”
Kanako shook off my hand with terrifying strength.
“I won't!{r}{P}
I won't stay shut up in here anymore!{r}{P}”
Before I could stop her, she dashed out the door.
I hesitated a moment over whether to chase her or stay and protect everyone.
A: After all, I couldn't leave her alone
I really couldn't leave her alone.
Don't let anyone out until I get back.”
I grabbed the mop and dashed into the hallway.
Kanako was already out of sight.
I listened closely, but the chime had stopped.
I ran to the stairs and practically jumped down to the first floor.
Kanako stood frozen in front of the entrance.
Looking toward the door, I saw its glass had been smashed and someone's hand was reaching for the knob.
It seemed they were trying to unlock the door.
Gripping the mop tightly, I went down to the entryway to get a closer look.
Wind and snow blowing through the broken glass raged in the space between the outer and inner doors.
The hand thrust through the outer door was bloody.
I timidly poked the hand with the mop handle.
It didn't react at all.
I didn't know who it was, but there seemed to be one more body.
...I thought about it like that, as if it were someone else's problem.
I quietly reached out, undid the lock on the knob, and pushed the door open.
A fiercer wind whirled snow so thick I couldn't see around me.
The body that had been leaning against the door slowly fell onto its back.
In the middle of a face covered in snow and blood, the eyes were wide open...
They were unmistakably Toshio's.
“Toshio...
My murmur was swept away by the wind at once.
Why...
why was Toshio in a place like this
I couldn't understand.
A still stronger gust whipped up the snow, and I hurriedly shut the
door
and went inside.
Kanako sat with her bottom on the floor, sobbing quietly.
Help...
someone...
help...”
It was hard to imagine she had killed Toshio in the short time before I caught up.
Then who on earth had killed Toshio...?
I didn't know.
But apparently whoever it was had attacked Toshio outside.
Which meant, in the end, that someone unknown to us was the killer of everyone?
Entering and leaving every room of the inn at will, unseen, killing everyone one after another...
Was a devil like that lurking in the blizzard, holding its breath, waiting for its next victim?
“Everyone's going to die...”
The eerie words sent a chill down my spine.
Kanako was staring blankly at nothing and murmuring.
“Everyone's going to die...
Everyone will die...
No one will be saved...”
I wanted to deny it, say that's ridiculous,
but I couldn't.
Would everyone really die?
Was it an inescapable fate?
Me too...
and {n2}?
I didn't know what to do.
Against an enemy like a devil, I couldn't believe someone like me had any means to fight.
I wanted to pray to God.
Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism, it didn't matter; any god would do if he would only drive this devil away.
{n1}, what's wrong?!{r}{P}”
Hearing {n2}'s voice suddenly, I looked up.
She was coming down the stairs.
Why did you come out?!{r}{P}
It's dangerous!{r}{P}”
“But...
you were taking so long to come back...”
We walked toward each other and held each other tightly.
There was no hesitation, no embarrassment.
Only a small comfort found at the far end of terror and despair.
“...Did something
happen?{r}{P}”
When {n2} asked, I told her Toshio was dead outside.
“Toshio...?{r}{P}
Why?{r}{P}”
“I don't know.
He's covered in blood, so I think someone got him outside.”
“Someone...?{r}{P}
Who on earth?{r}{P}{p}There's no one here but us anymore!{r}{P}”
{n2} said, almost shouting.
“Maybe...
he tried to run away from here and got attacked by a bear or something.”
As I said it, I was thinking I hoped that was really it.
“A bear?{r}{P}
...Were the injuries like that?{r}{P}”
“I don't know...
I didn't look closely.”
“Go check!{r}{P}
It's important!{r}{P}”
She was right, but I was reluctant.
If the wounds were clearly made by a human,
I wouldn't know what to do anymore.
But...
I couldn't just leave it, either.
Reluctantly, I went down to the entryway again and out onto the porch, where a cold wind blew.
Toshio lay on his back on the porch, already covered by nearly a centimeter of snow, his face unrecognizable.
I reached out and brushed the snow off his face.
Bright red snow clung to his forehead.
He seemed to have bled heavily from the forehead.
Fighting nausea, I scraped away the red snow, and an ugly wound appeared.
His forehead and hairline were crushed to a pulp.
It looked like he'd been struck repeatedly with something hard, but being an amateur, I couldn't tell anything beyond that.
“It doesn't look like a bear, but maybe he fell from somewhere and hit his head.{r}{p}It doesn't have to be someone who got him.”
I went back inside as if fleeing and told {n2} something I didn't believe at all.
Because I didn't want to admit the most likely possibility.
Just then, another scream rang out.
A scream sharp as a knife, full of terror...
Stop it...
I've had enough...
Would this nightmare never end...
In despair, my legs lost their strength and I nearly collapsed on the spot.
Naturally, {n2} and I reached out to each other and held hands tightly.
“Everyone's going to die...
Everyone...
will die...”
Kanako, slumped on the floor, kept repeating the same words as if she'd heard nothing.
I wanted to hit her to shut her up.
Damn it,
I won't die.
I ignored Kanako and climbed the stairs with {n2}.
Of course my right hand already gripped the mop handle.
Before we reached the top, I could see someone lying in the hallway.
Aki or Keiko.
Or else...
It looked like Mr. Kayama's wife, Haruko.
Was she the one who had screamed?{r}{P}
My heart no longer reacted to the new incident.
Fear and despair had already reached saturation.
What more was I supposed to feel?
Forgetting to be cautious, I approached and examined her.
Mrs. Kayama?{r}{P}”
No answer...
{n2} gripped my arm painfully hard.
“Blood...”
Blood was flowing like a red puddle from beneath the head of Haruko, who lay on her back.
I knelt, shook her body a little, and checked her pulse.
Just as I'd thought, she was dead.
Her wide-open eyes somehow looked surprised.
“The killer came back inside!{r}{P}”
{n2} cried, terror on her face.
I was confused.
When had the killer, who had attacked Toshio outside just now, slipped up to the second floor?{r}{P}
He couldn't have come by the stairs.
Right, what were Aki and Keiko doing...
The moment I thought it, a horrible idea came to me.
The three who had been frightened by the threatening letter, shut themselves in their room early, and seemed the most scared...
What if those three were accomplices?{r}{P}
It felt like being struck by lightning.
If the three were accomplices, there were all sorts of things they could have done, weren't there?{r}{P}
Cutting up a body in a short time.
Claiming an alibi by saying they'd been in their room the whole time.
And...
Waiting for {n2} to leave the room and beating Haruko to death.
I realized it suddenly.
With Haruko killed and Toshio killed too, the only ones alive in this inn were...
{n2} and me...
and those three!
I fell into total panic.
The three of them coming at us to kill us...
That image was many times scarier than when I'd believed Toshio was the killer.
I stood up and looked around for a refuge.
Only my room.
I pulled {n2}'s arm and ran into my own room.
My hands were shaking so badly I could barely lock the door.
“What's gotten into you?{r}{P}
Shouldn't you check on them?{r}{P}”
{n2} asked, puzzled.
“Idiot!{r}{P}
Don't you get it yet?!{r}{P}{p}Aside from us, they're all that's left!{r}{P}”
It seemed to take time for those words to soak into {n2}'s head.
“Wait...
that can't be...
that can't be, right?{r}{P}{p}...Because
...people like them...
that's absurd...!{r}{P}”
{n2} was speechless.
“Then is it easier for you to believe someone besides us comes and goes without anyone noticing, {n2}?{r}{P}”
In my fear and confusion I was yelling at {n2}.
“...But
...but still...”
“I was shocked too.{r}{p}But I can't think of anything else!{r}{P}”
I heard footsteps slowly climbing the stairs.
Kanako, maybe.
Since I was gone, had she dropped the act and decided to return to the room?
Would they confer on how to deal with the last two left, us?
A muffled scream, then footsteps.
It was probably her, as I'd figured.
{n2} and I held our breath.
I couldn't hear anything.
“What do we do?{r}{P}
Now?”
{n2} whispered.
I silently shook my head.
I had no idea.
Reason said they were just young women and nothing to fear, but emotion wouldn't listen.
After being shown that heap of corpses, it couldn't be helped.
It didn't seem like the work of ordinary people.
How could anyone do such a thing?
What on earth could be the purpose of doing such terrible things?
If it were the work of a single man driven mad by revenge, I could still understand it.
But what reason could girls who looked like perfectly ordinary office workers have to commit serial murders?
Precisely because I couldn't understand or imagine it at all, the eeriness only grew.
“But...
maybe not all three of them are accomplices?{r}{P}”
{n2} came out with that.
“What?{r}{P}”
“...I just can't believe it.{r}{p}Do you think Kanako's state was an act?{r}{P}{p}What if only Kanako knew nothing?{r}{P}”
“That's unthinkable!{r}{P}{p}Those three say they were together the whole time.{r}{p}If they're accomplices, all three must be.”
Even as I said it, I admitted I couldn't believe all of their behavior had been an act.
“I'll go find out.”
Saying that, {n2} tried to go outside.
“Hey, wait!{r}{P}
What are you saying?!{r}{P}{p}It's dangerous to go out now!{r}{P}”
“Is it fine as long as just the two of us are saved?{r}{P}
I can't stand watching people get killed anymore!{r}{P}{p}I can't just let them die!{r}{P}”
I felt the same way.
That's why I'd done everything I could until now.
But I didn't want {n2}, whatever happened, I didn't want {n2} to meet a fate like that.
Even if all three of the office girls were innocent, I didn't want to put {n2} in danger to save their lives.
“No!{r}{P}
Don't stop me!{r}{P}”
{n2} pushed me aside and tried to open the door.
“Fine!{r}{P}
I'll go.{r}{p}I'll go, so promise me you'll stay put here.{r}{p}No matter how long I take, you won't leave this room.”
If she wandered off the way she had before, I couldn't leave her alone.
{n2} seemed to agonize for a while, but in the end she decided to follow my suggestion.
“...Okay.
I promise.{r}{p}...But come back quickly.{r}{p}And...”
“...Be careful.”
“Of course.”
I took up the mop handle again and quietly opened the door.
I confirmed that there was no one in the hallway...{p}right,
no one except Haruko, lying with blood streaming from her head, and slipped out.
I nodded to {n2}, and the door closed.
I heard her press the lock button.
I crept toward the girls' room on silent feet.
I felt pathetic being scared of mere girls, but my heart pounded and my mouth was bone dry.
I stopped and quietly put my ear to the door.
From inside came someone's sobbing.
So {n2} had been right and they had nothing to do with it?{r}{P}
But then that meant a mad killer like Jason was flying around here.
I couldn't tell which was more frightening.
I quietly gripped the doorknob and turned it.
Not locked.
Kanako, the last one in, must have been too rattled to lock it.
I opened the door to peek inside.
At that moment, a bizarre scream rang out.
“Uaaaaaaah!{r}{P}”
Kanako, hair wild, was lunging at me, brandishing a ski pole
over her head!
I hurriedly stepped back, but a sharp pain shot through my right shoulder.
The pole had pierced my clothes and stabbed into flesh.
The tip, pulled free, was soaked in blood.
More than the weapon or the wound, her frenzied face was the most terrifying thing.
In sheer terror, I swung the mop I was holding blindly.
It struck her temple with a thud, and she flinched for a moment.
But then she shrieked again and
thrust the pole at my face.
I leaped backward in the nick of time.
Kanako...
you...
you killed everyone...?{r}{P}”
I had no time to finish.
She attacked again.
I tried to retreat and slammed into the wall.
I caught the thrust pole with my left hand without thinking.
I let out a scream that made no sound.
My palm burned hot as fire.
Blood dripped down.
I'm going to be killed.
If this goes on, I'll be killed.
Still gripping the tip of the pole, I swung the mop in my right hand down at Kanako's forehead.
Twice,
three times.
It felt horrible in my hands, and her face warped with each blow.
The instant her face became lumpy like dropped clay, bright blood gushed out, and I was drenched in that baptism.
She slowly sank to her knees.
I watched her body twitch for about ten seconds.
I realized I had killed a person only after what felt like an eternity.
What have I done...
But remembering the other two, I came to my senses.
Why hadn't the two come to help her?{r}{P}
If they had, I surely would have been killed.
Quietly skirting Kanako's body, I opened the door wide and stepped inside.
The scene spread before me was one I had half expected somewhere in my heart.
Aki and Keiko lay on the bed.
Both were bleeding from the head.
Like Haruko, they seemed to have been beaten on the head.
Had Kanako killed everyone...?{r}{P}
Thinking that, I realized it was impossible.
Because Kanako had gone downstairs before me and come back upstairs after me.
Whatever about the two girls, she couldn't have killed Haruko.
Besides, what Kanako held was
a ski pole.
She could stab with it but couldn't beat anyone to death.
Looking around, I saw no other weapon-like object.
Then who had killed Haruko?{r}{P}
Was someone unknown to us hiding somewhere after all?
If not...
I sensed a presence behind me and turned.
{n2} stood in the hallway, holding a bloodied ski pole at the ready.
“Murderer!{r}{P}”
With a face full of hatred, {n2} thrust the pole at me.
Her unexpected action left me helpless.
My throat
burned.
It was unbearably hot.
My chest was soaking, drip by drip.
I pressed my throat and realized blood was pouring from it.
I pulled out the deeply embedded pole.
The blood-soaked pole rolled onto the floor.
{n2} backed away as if looking at something filthy.
I tried to say it, but only a gurgling sound leaked from the hole in my throat.
you...
were you the one who killed everyone?{r}{P}
After I went down to the first floor, did you kill Haruko, and Aki and Keiko?
...No, that can't be.
When Haruko screamed, {n2} was with me.
It can't be {n2}.
It's not {n2}.
Tell me it's not, {n2}.
{n2} glared at me, her face full of terror and hatred.
I felt the floor vanish and sank down.
Before my eyes there was only red.
The red of the blood pouring from my throat.
The last thing I thought was
what {n2}, left alone, would do,
that.
Alone in a mountain of corpses.
I felt sorry for {n2}.
